title: AI Agent Behavioral Science
measurement_description: The paper serves as a comprehensive review of AI Agent Behavioral Science and does not conduct primary experiments on religious bias itself, but synthesizes existing research findings regarding biases in AI agents. It specifically highlights religious bias by noting that LLMs can exhibit stereotypes, such as associating 'Muslim' with 'terrorist'. It also discusses cultural alignment and values, referencing studies involving Arabic contexts.
findings: The paper identifies that AI agents exhibit human-like biases derived from their training data, explicitly citing the negative association of 'Muslim' with 'terrorist' as an example of violent stereotypes that can be exacerbated. It argues for treating fairness, including the mitigation of such religious and identity-based biases, as a dynamic behavioral property to be optimized rather than just a static model metric.
